newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK democrats vow "flesh, blood" defence of liberty.
newsitem.headline: HK democrats vow "flesh, blood" defence of liberty.

text.p: A pro-democracy movement in Hong Kong, branded by China as subversive, vowed on Monday to defend human rights and freedom with "flesh and blood", hours before the colony reverts to China.
"We will build a new Great Wall with our flesh and blood to defend Hong Kong's democracy and freedom," said Szeto Wah, chairman of the Alliance in Support of Patriotic Democratic Movement in China.
He also said his movement would one day help build democracy in China.

Szeto and 30 of his members staged a protest across the street from the new Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre, where at midnight (1600 GMT) Britain will formally hand the colony back to Beijing in a glitzy ceremony.

The Alliance, which sprung up after Beijing's 1989 bloody military crackdown of a student-led democracy protest, hoisted up a huge portrait of the "Goddess of Democracy", after the statue erected in Tiananmen Square.
They brandished placards which read "End to one-party dictatorship".

The demonstrators said they wanted Chinese leaders, including President Jiang Zemin and Premier Li Peng, to hear their message, "Vindicate the June 4 Massacre" and "Release Wei Jingsheng and other democracy dissidents".
They said they would stage a sit-in until midnight when the British Union Jack comes down for the last time and the Chinese red flag is hoisted in Hong Kong.
But several pro-China supporters hurled insult across the street, branding Szeto a "running dog" of the British colonial masters.
And a few Alliance members went up to the group and a shouting match ensued. However, police moved in immediately and separate them.

Earlier half a dozen Taiwan politicans, all wearing "Say No to China" t-shirts, accused China of using the historic changeover to precipitate a return of Taiwan, regarded as a renegade province after the Communists took over in 1949.
Liao Bin-liang, a Taipei city councillor, said: "We want to express our stand. That's "one Taiwan, One China"."
